epic.intent:
## Outcome
A person can call up a **Cult**: one lead agent, the **Magos**, that they talk to in an ordinary terminal chat, plus as many lower-tier **Acolyte** agents as the Magos summons. A cult can be a test swarm on a repository or something playful, such as continuously drawing a plant named Gerry as it grows. The person can start, pause, resume and stop a cult at will. Every run has a time limit. When the limit runs out, the Magos shuts the cult down gracefully and then ends itself.

The design follows Anthropic's Claude Code *agent teams* (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams):

| Agent teams | Cults |
| --- | --- |
| team lead | Magos |
| teammates | Acolytes |
| per-member mailbox | the Skitarii mailbox |
| lead picks teammate models | the Magos picks each acolyte's model, cheapest first |
| shutdown request that a teammate approves | the cult's shutdown protocol |

It departs from agent teams in three places:
- The app, not the agent, enforces the time limit, the acolyte cap, pause and the hard backstop.
- A person can watch acolytes but cannot type to them.
- Each cult has a Shrine that shows what the cult makes.

## User journeys
1. **Found a cult.** In the sidebar's new CULTS section, below AGENTS, press `+`. Enter a name and a charter (what the cult is for). Choose a tracked folder, or none for a project-less cult. Give the Magos a name (a themed name is suggested) and choose its model from the models OMP is signed in to. Set a time limit typed as a duration (`30m` by default, or `90hr`, `2d`, `1d 6h`), or tick **Unlimited**. Set an acolyte cap (default 6). Under Advanced timings, optionally change the shutdown timings. The cult is saved and can be started again later.
2. **Start and talk.** Start creates a new run. A Skitarii (OMP) terminal chat opens for the Magos with the charter and the cult rules, and the person chats with it like any agent.
3. **Acolytes.** The Magos summons acolytes, each a separate OMP chat with a unique **name** (the Magos names it, or the app generates a themed name), a mission and a model. Every cultist is shown by name everywhere: sidebar, terminal headers, the pipeline, the Cult page. By default an acolyte gets the cheapest model OMP is signed in to. The Magos may pick a higher tier, but only with a reason, which the acolyte's row shows. Acolytes appear under the cult's run in the sidebar, following the pattern of the expandable agent rows from DM-619. Their terminals are **watch-only**.
4. **Petitions.** The Magos must ask the person through a **petition** for three things:
   - more acolytes than the cap;
   - **Allow save** (saving plans);
   - orchestrator access to **another tracked folder**.

   Each petition waits on the Cult page with its reason, and the person approves or denies it. An approved petition takes effect on the running Magos without a restart and is revoked when the run ends. A petition still unanswered when the run ends counts as denied. The person can also raise the cap at any time.
5. **Pipeline.** The Cult page's comms pane has a Pipeline tab that shows the cult's pipeline: every message between cultists and every run event (summons, petitions, pause, shutdown, Shrine), by name, live, as read-only plain text.
6. **Pause and resume.** Pause interrupts every member's current turn, stops all wake-ups and freezes the timer. Resume continues.
7. **Stop and expiry.** Stop, or the time running out, starts the graceful shutdown: the Magos orders the acolytes to conclude, they report and exit within the grace window (default 3 m), the Magos writes the run's chronicle (a summary) within its window (default 2 m) and exits, and the app force-ends anything still alive at the hard backstop (grace + window + 1 m). **Kill now** ends everything immediately.
8. **Shrine.** A cult can publish an image (PNG, JPEG or SVG) or an HTML page from its working directory. The Cult page shows the latest one, sandboxed, and updates it live. This is how Gerry is seen growing.

## Confirmed decisions (by the person)
- A cult is a reusable definition with runs. Past runs keep their chronicles.
- Where a cult works is chosen per cult: a tracked folder, or a project-less app-owned directory.
- Pause is soft: it interrupts turns, holds wake-ups and freezes the timer. Processes and context survive.
- The timer counts only running time, not paused time. Expiry runs the graceful shutdown, the hard backstop then force-ends what is left, and quitting the app marks a running run `interrupted`. The default limit is 30 minutes. A limit is typed as any duration of at least 1 minute (`1m`, `90hr`, `2d`), with no upper bound, or set to **Unlimited**, in which case only Stop or Kill now ends the run.
- Shutdown timings: acolyte grace 3 minutes, Magos window 2 minutes, backstop = grace + window + 1 minute. These are defaults, customizable per cult and per run.
- The acolyte cap defaults to 6. The Magos may petition for more; only the person approves; an unanswered petition counts as denied.
- Communication uses the **Skitarii mailbox** from the Skitarii communications epic. Every Magos and acolyte is therefore a Skitarii (OMP) chat. Models come from the providers OMP is signed in to (`omp models` / `omp usage --json`).
- Waking members: starting a run grants a **standing wake** limited to that run, Magos to acolyte and acolyte to Magos. Pause, stop, expiry and quit revoke it. Everywhere else the mailbox's one-shot human wake rule still applies.
- Acolyte models: the cheapest signed-in model by default. A higher tier needs a stated reason, which is shown in the UI. No approval is needed.
- Acolytes are watch-only for the person.
- The Shrine panel is in scope.
- A folder cult shares the folder. The Magos is told to split work by file.
- The Magos gets an **orchestrator** grant on its workspace. Save rights are available but **must be petitioned**: Allow save is off until the person approves an `allow_save` petition. In a project-less cult the grant covers only the sanctum, and the Magos may petition for orchestrator access to a specific tracked folder.
- Acolytes hold a `worker` grant, because the mailbox requires one of the hosted roles. They have no assigned attempts, so they cannot change plans.
- Several cults may run at once. Each cult definition has at most one active run.
- Cult member chats are hidden from a folder's ordinary chat list and from DM-619's agent rows. They appear only under CULTS.
- All chatter is visible in the cult pipeline, and every cultist has a unique display name.
- Deleting a cult ends any active run and deletes its runs, member chats, transcripts and sanctum.
- An interrupted run is not resumed; the person starts a new run.
- Standards: the Definition of Done only.

## Assumptions (provisional)
- The bounds on customizable shutdown timings are 30 seconds to 60 minutes each.
- Raising the cap has an absolute ceiling of 24 acolytes per run, to bound process count and cost.
- A folder-access petition grants orchestrator access without Allow save. Saving in that folder needs its own `allow_save` petition, which covers the cult's workspace only.

## Scope
Cult definitions and runs (app-level), the run supervisor (lifecycle, timer, pause, shutdown, backstop, restart reconciliation), the OMP signed-in model catalog with cheapest-first tiers, agent-facing cult commands, petitions with live grant upgrades, the run-scoped standing wake and Skitarii native cult tools, typed desktop IPC, the cult pipeline, the CULTS sidebar section, the Cult page with controls, watch-only acolyte terminals, the Shrine, and documentation.

## Non-goals
- Non-OMP Magos or acolytes, and extending the mailbox to other CLIs.
- The person typing into acolyte terminals.
- A shared task list or claimable cult tasks; the Magos coordinates over the mailbox.
- Per-acolyte Git worktrees.
- Messaging across folders or machines, and broadcast outside a cult. (A Magos's `order_all` to the acolytes of its own run is in scope; see The chamber.)
- Sound of any kind.
- A top-down or isometric room, a new movement engine, or a custom chat UI for the Magos.
- OS-level process suspension.
- Resuming an interrupted run.
- Cost accounting beyond showing each acolyte's model and tier.
- A marketplace or templates of cults.

## Entry dependencies
This epic builds on two pieces of work that must be merged into the default branch before its run starts:
- **Skitarii communications** epic (`ep_01m6t9cg507rmyg2q9nsw7kv3s`), currently in progress: the mailbox store, API and binding are accepted; DM-510 to DM-514 are open. Cults uses its mailbox, its shell-free `dmClient`, its native tools and its desktop wake bridge.
- Kanban card **DM-619**, currently in progress: expandable agent rows, the project-less chat directory and the cross-folder chat listing. CULTS follows its pattern.

The first ticket re-verifies both against the merged code before anything is built on them.

## Standards
The project Definition of Done only, run once at the acceptance node. Each ticket writes and runs the tests its **Tests** section lists, plus lint and typecheck when it changes code. No tests-first and no Fireguard grading. Electron isolation and typed, guarded IPC are preserved.

## Platforms
Windows is the verification platform. macOS and Linux code paths are unit-tested only, and the documentation says so.

## The chamber (revision 3, from the person)
The Cult page is a **Mechanicus chamber**, not a panel of lists. The person watches the cult as a little scene and talks to the Magos beside it.

### Layout
- **Command bar** across the top: name, state, the countdown (frozen while paused, or Unlimited with elapsed time), Start (with per-run overrides), Pause/Resume, Stop, Kill now, cap with Raise, and a Past runs button.
- **The room** on the left: a painted **side-view cross-section** of a Mechanicus chamber (backdrop, consoles, a teleport pad, a blast door, and a **viewscreen** on the back wall that shows the Shrine, with Enlarge).
- **The Magos at the helm** at the room's right edge, on a raised command pulpit facing into the room, joined by a glowing conduit to the comms pane beside it.
- **Comms pane** on the right, with tabs: **Magos** (his real, interactive OMP terminal, the default tab), **Pipeline**, and a closable watch-only terminal tab per acolyte that the person opens.
- **Petitions** appear as scroll banners over the top of the room with Approve and Deny, while the Magos holds a petition scroll up toward the person.
- A keyboard-accessible **roster strip** under the room (member chips). Clicking a sprite or a chip opens an **inspector** card: name, role, model, tier, reason, state, latest activity, Watch terminal and Dismiss.
- A **Past runs** drawer holds the run history and chronicles. With no active run, the room is dark and empty.

### Characters
- **Magos**: a new character in the mascot's painted chibi style (`build/mechanicus-cute-master.png`), larger and more senior (mechadendrites, a staff of office). He has seven new 6-frame atlases: idle at the helm, speak (while his terminal is busy), order one, order all, summon, petition, and chronicle (writes on a data-slate, then bows or powers down).
- **Acolytes**: the existing chibi tech-priest. Each acolyte gets a robe tint (CSS hue rotation, which also shifts the lenses; the person accepted that), a name plate, and the same member colour in the pipeline and the roster. They reuse the seven existing atlases plus two new ones, **salute** (receiving an order) and **type** (working at a console). Idle acolytes goof around on the existing seeded engine (`mascot/motion.ts`), with consoles as platforms: they wander, jump, climb and stumble. Working acolytes go to a console and type. Extras beyond the consoles drill.
- **Speech bubbles**, as plain text: live activity from OMP (tool and target, phrased in a Mechanicus voice), the first line of mail when it is sent or received, and canned goofy quips while idle. There is no agent-authored status tool.

### Orders and reports
- **Targeted order** (Magos to one acolyte): the Magos plays order one, a glowing binharic packet arcs to the acolyte, and the acolyte jumps with a "!" and salutes.
- **Order to all**: a new Magos command `order_all` (native tool `cult_order_all`) sends one mailbox message to each live acolyte of its run under a shared order id recorded as one `order_all` cult event. The Magos raises his staff, and a noosphere ring sweeps the room; each acolyte salutes as the ring reaches it.
- **Reports** (acolyte to Magos) send a packet back, and the Magos speaks briefly. Acolyte-to-acolyte mail sends a packet between them.

### Run-state theatrics
- Pause: stasis. Everyone freezes mid-pose, the room desaturates and a STASIS overlay appears; Resume continues from the same poses.
- Graceful shutdown: acolytes deliver report packets and march out the blast door; the Magos writes the chronicle and the lights dim.
- Kill now: an instant blackout with sparks.
- The last minute of a timed run pulses warning lights.
- Summon: the acolyte beams in on the teleport pad. Dismiss: it walks out the door.

### Motion, accessibility and performance
- One frame loop drives every sprite. It stops while the page is hidden or the room is off-screen.
- With reduced motion, the room is static: members stand at fixed spots, there is no travel or effects, and bubbles and states still update.
- The scene is decorative (`aria-hidden`). The roster, inspector, banners and command bar carry every fact and control.

### Art
All new art is generated with an image-generation tool, the way the mascot was (`docs/mascot-sprites.md`), from the master reference. There are no hand-painted edits and no vector stand-ins. The art tickets need a worker host with an image-generation tool.

## Cult archetypes and specialist acolytes (revision 4, confirmed by the person)
A cult has an **archetype** and every acolyte has a user-visible **worker type**. Worker type is professional perspective; it is separate from the Dark Mechanicus grant role, model, tier, display name and ticket `workType`.

### Built-in cult archetypes
| Archetype | Purpose | Default council |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **General** | A free-form swarm for any charter. | No required worker types; the Magos chooses. |
| **Plan Forge** | Build or review one specific Dark Mechanicus epic plan. | Six required, distinct specialists: UI/UX, implementation engineering, delivery/Scrum, security, quality, and architecture/team lead. |
| **Delivery** | Deliver a bounded implementation charter. | Architecture/team lead, implementation engineering, quality and delivery/Scrum; editable before founding. |
| **Audit / Red Team** | Challenge a product, plan or change without implementing it. | Security, quality, architecture/team lead and implementation engineering; analysis-only charter. |
| **Research / Creative** | Explore, prototype or create an artifact such as the Gerry Shrine. | UI/UX, implementation engineering and quality; editable before founding. |
| **Custom** | Use a person-defined council. | The person names required worker slots and their missions. |

Built-in rosters other than Plan Forge are editable defaults. Plan Forge's six perspectives are mandatory and cannot be removed or merged. The acolyte cap cannot be below the required-slot count.

### Worker types
- **UI/UX**: journeys, information architecture, interaction, accessibility and visual evidence.
- **Implementation engineering**: source architecture, interfaces, dependencies, feasibility and implementation risks.
- **Delivery/Scrum**: scope, ticket boundaries, graph, sequencing, resource risk and likelihood of success.
- **Security**: authority, trust boundaries, privacy, abuse cases, unsafe defaults and mitigations.
- **Quality**: acceptance, deterministic tests, end-to-end proof, failure cases and release evidence.
- **Architecture/team lead**: boundaries, integration, tradeoffs, maintainability and conflicts between recommendations.
- Custom cults may add named custom worker types; standard identifiers remain stable for filtering and reports.

### Plan Forge protocol
1. A Plan Forge cult requires a tracked folder and target epic. Its run records the target epic id and the draft/saved revision it began from.
2. The Magos summons one distinct acolyte for each mandatory worker type. Duplicate coverage does not fill another slot. Each mission carries the same target and a specialist contract.
3. Each specialist independently reads the plan and submits evidence, risks, recommendations, acceptance/verification impact and blockers. Acolytes can read the target but cannot edit its draft or save it.
4. The Magos waits for all six reports, resolves disagreements explicitly rather than voting, records accepted and rejected recommendations with reasons, edits the target draft and validates it.
5. The app refuses Plan Forge conclusion while a report is missing or the target draft is stale or invalid.
6. Only the Magos edits the draft. Save still requires an approved **Allow save** petition. Without approval, the validated draft remains unsaved for the person to review.

### Confirmed revision 4 decisions
- Initial catalog: General, Plan Forge, Delivery, Audit / Red Team, Research / Creative and Custom.
- Plan Forge uses six distinct required acolytes; specialties are not combined.
- Acolytes submit independent findings; the Magos owns conflict resolution and synthesis.
- The Magos may edit the targeted draft, but Save remains human-gated through Allow save.

## Magos-created worker types (revision 5, confirmed by the person)
The built-in catalog is a floor, not a closed taxonomy. During any active run, the Magos may identify a missing perspective, define a **run-scoped worker type**, and inject an acolyte of that type.

- `create_worker_type` records a unique name, description, mission/review contract, rationale and whether its report is required for conclusion. The app assigns the stable run-local id; the Magos cannot choose or impersonate a built-in id.
- The type exists only for that run. It remains in run history and the chronicle but does not silently mutate the reusable cult definition or global catalog.
- The Magos injects it by calling `summon_acolyte` with the new type id. Normal model selection, acolyte cap, higher-tier reason, petition, pause and shutdown rules still apply.
- A created type changes specialization metadata and prompt content only. It never grants tools, folders, Save, a stronger Dark Mechanicus role, a model upgrade or any other authority.
- Built-in names and ids cannot be shadowed. Names, descriptions, missions and rationales are bounded inert text. At most 24 run-scoped types may exist, matching the absolute acolyte ceiling.
- A type marked required is immutable for that run and blocks conclusion until one assigned acolyte submits its report. Optional types do not gate conclusion and may be retired only before an acolyte is assigned. Every create/retire/summon action is a cult event.
- In Plan Forge, the six standard perspectives remain mandatory. Magos-created types are additive and can never replace, merge or satisfy those six slots; a required additional type joins the synthesis gate.

bundle.rationale:
## Approach
The design models Claude Code agent teams: the lead is the Magos, the teammates are acolytes, and the mailbox carries their messages. The app, not the agent, owns time, the cap, pause and the backstop, because an LLM cannot be relied on to stop itself. Cults are app-level records (app.sqlite), because a cult can be project-less. Every member is an ordinary Skitarii chat, so the mailbox, grants, terminals and transcripts are reused unchanged. A project-less cult gets an app-owned sanctum workspace, so the per-folder machinery (mailbox endpoints, grants, chat stores) works without a parallel implementation. Agent-facing commands reuse the nameChat control-pipe pattern, and authority comes only from the bound grant.

## Rejected alternatives
- A cult-owned paste channel that types into terminals: rejected by the person, who chose the mailbox, and it conflicts with the mailbox's no-PTY-typing rule.
- Any CLI kind as a member: the mailbox is OMP-only, and OMP reaches every signed-in provider through one CLI.
- OS process suspension for pause: in-flight API calls break, and it is risky on Windows.
- Per-acolyte Git worktrees: the person chose a shared folder, with the Magos splitting work by file.
- A shared task list: the Magos coordinates over the mailbox instead (non-goal).

## Graph
One sprint, because the deliverable is a usable cult; any interim checkpoint would split it by layer.
- Row 1: the investigation (OMP control points, sanctum feasibility, entry check) and the store, in parallel.
- Then: models and launch → supervise → (bridge and tools in parallel) → (side after bridge, wake after tools) → page → (pipeline and shrine in parallel, each after page and wake) → docs.
- Critical path: inv → launch → supervise → bridge → side → page → shrine or pipeline → docs.
- The investigation gates every OMP-dependent ticket. If it finds a control point infeasible, the orchestrator redrafts the dependent ticket before claiming it.

## Risks and mitigations
- Runaway processes or cost: the app enforces the cap (default 6, ceiling 24), the time limit and the hard backstop, startup reconciliation marks leftover runs interrupted, and the default model is the cheapest tier.
- Widened wake authority: one predicate, scoped to the run and to members only, closed on pause or end, with tests for every outside case.
- A sanctum bypass that admits arbitrary untracked paths: one trusted predicate admits only registered sanctums, and a test proves other paths are still refused.
- Agent-authored HTML in the app: a sandbox with only allow-scripts, an opaque origin, a CSP with no network, served only for the run's published path.
- The dependency epics are not landed yet: entry criteria, and the investigation re-verifies them.

## Assumptions
The remaining assumptions are listed in the epic intent: timing bounds of 30 s to 60 m, a cap ceiling of 24, and folder-access petitions granting no Allow save.

## Revision 2 decisions (from the person)
- Save rights are available but must be petitioned.
- A project-less Magos is scoped to its sanctum and can petition for a folder.
- Acolytes hold worker grants.
- Shutdown timings are defaults and customizable.
- Time limits accept any duration of at least 1 minute, or Unlimited.
- Several cults may run at once.
- Member chats appear only under CULTS, with all chatter in a named pipeline (a new ticket).
- Deleting a cult cascades.
- Interrupted runs are not resumed.


## Revision 3 decisions (from the person): the chamber
The person redesigned the Cult page as a Mechanicus chamber. Decided in two rounds of questions:
- **A side-view cross-section**, not top-down or isometric. It reuses `mascot/motion.ts` (the seeded wander, jump, climb and stumble engine) with consoles as platforms, plus all seven acolyte atlases. A top-down room would need a new engine and 4-direction art.
- **The right pane is the Magos's real OMP terminal**, with Pipeline and watch-only acolyte tabs. A custom chat UI was rejected: it would need TUI parsing or a second channel.
- **Layout**: a top command bar; the Shrine as a back-wall viewscreen with Enlarge; petition scroll banners with the Magos holding a scroll; a roster strip plus an inspector; a Past runs drawer; a dark room with no run.
- **Bubbles**: OMP activity (structured in main, phrased in the renderer), the first line of mail, and idle quips. A `cult_say` agent-status tool was rejected for its token cost and unreliability.
- **Order to all**: a new `order_all` command and `cult_order_all` tool that fan out over the mailbox and record one `order_all` event. This lifts the broadcast non-goal for a Magos's own run only. A timing heuristic was rejected as nondeterministic.
- **The helm is at the right edge**, beside the comms pane, joined by a conduit.
- **Magos art**: seven atlases (idle, speak, order one, order all, summon, petition, chronicle). Targeted orders are code-drawn binharic packets; reports animate back. Acolytes are robe-tinted by hue rotation (the person accepted the lens shift) and get new salute and type atlases.
- **Theatrics**: stasis, shutdown march with lights dim, Kill-now blackout, last-minute warning. No sound.
- **Art is generated by a worker host with an image-generation tool**, as the mascot's was. Code-drawn art was rejected because it would clash with the painted style.
- **All of it is in the existing single sprint.** A plain page followed by a chamber sprint would rebuild the page (a layer split).

### Graph changes
- The two art tickets and the chamber logic have no prerequisites, so they run in row 1 beside the investigation and the store.
- Scene requires both art tickets and the logic; effects require scene.
- Activity requires the IPC bridge (snapshot type); the page requires the sidebar and activity.
- Live chamber is the join: it requires effects, pipeline and Shrine (the page and activity arrive through those). Docs require live chamber.
- The critical path stays on the backend chain: investigation → launch → supervise → bridge → activity → page → pipeline → live chamber → docs. The art and the scene finish well off it.

### Risks
- **No host with an image-generation tool.** The art tickets carry the environment constraint and stop and report instead of drawing stand-ins. The orchestrator escalates this to the person, the only owner of that decision, before the art blocks the scene.
- **Generated props do not give clean standable tops or a clean screen window.** `props.json` is measured from alpha and tested, and layout reads only measured rects.
- **Frame cost with many sprites.** There is one loop, guarded by visibility, intersection and reduced motion, and a measured trace at 12 acolytes is acceptance evidence.
- **Duplicate or replayed animations after polling.** The feed is idempotent by snapshot revision and pipeline sequence, and is tested.
- **The activity source may be thinner than hoped** (investigation question 8). Activity then falls back to working or idle only, and the orchestrator decides.

## Revision 4 decisions: archetypes and multidisciplinary planning
The previous plan had only a free-form charter and arbitrary missions. It could produce a planning swarm with six engineering agents and no product, delivery, security or quality challenge. The selected design adds a small built-in catalog and stable worker types while retaining Custom for unusual councils.

Plan Forge is stricter than the other presets. Its six distinct reports are an application-enforced quorum, not prompt-only advice. The Magos is the sole synthesizer because concurrent plan edits create draft conflicts and erase decision ownership. Acolytes are independent readers/reporters; the Magos records disagreements, edits one draft and validates it. Save remains behind Allow save.

Rejected alternatives: General-plus-Plan-Forge only (too little vocabulary), custom-only (recreates safe rosters every time), combined specialties (hides missing perspectives), proposal-only Magos (manual transcription), and shared acolyte edits (collisions and diffuse accountability). Ticket capability `workType` is not reused because dispatch work and professional perspective are different concepts.

### Graph changes
- A pure contract ticket defines archetypes, worker types and roster validation before persistence.
- Existing persistence, launch, control, IPC and UI tickets carry the metadata end to end.
- A separate Plan Forge council ticket follows cult commands and precedes IPC, keeping quorum, reports, staleness and validation independently testable.
- The investigation proves the target-plan adapter and real read/edit/Save boundaries before Plan Forge integration is claimed.

### New risks and mitigations
- **Prompt-only role theater:** the store and conclusion gate require six distinct slots and six reports.
- **Stale target:** record the starting revision and reject conclusion until it is re-read.
- **Acolyte mutation:** verify worker capabilities; accept plan edits only from the bound Magos.
- **Rubber-stamp synthesis:** record accepted and rejected recommendations with reasons.
- **Preset sprawl:** all six archetypes use one roster contract and execution engine.

## Revision 5 decision: adaptive worker types
A fixed catalog cannot anticipate every domain: a plan may need localization, compliance, performance, data migration, game design or another specialist. The Magos therefore gets a bounded run-scoped extension mechanism.

Run scope is the safe default. It lets the Magos adapt immediately without permanently changing future runs or creating an unreviewed global taxonomy. A created type carries no authority; grants and model selection remain on existing paths. Built-in ids cannot be shadowed, the 24-type ceiling bounds state, and every change is visible in events and UI.

Plan Forge's six-person quorum stays intact. Dynamic specialists supplement it. Marking one required makes its report part of the conclusion gate and is irreversible for the run, preventing the Magos from deleting an inconvenient required perspective to conclude.

Epic Cults (read the epic intent). Every cult member is a Skitarii (OMP) chat in the app's PTY host. Cults need control points that nothing in the app uses yet. ## Entry check (do this first)
Confirm, in the checked-out branch, that the Skitarii communications epic (`ep_01m6t9cg507rmyg2q9nsw7kv3s`, DM-505..514) and Kanban card DM-619 have merged. If either has not merged, stop and report to the orchestrator: this is an entry blocker, not something to build around.

## Questions to answer, with evidence
1. **Interrupt a turn** (soft pause): the supported way to stop an OMP chat's in-flight turn without ending the process: an extension API (abort/cancel through the Skitarii extension), an OMP RPC, or a control keystroke written to the PTY (`terminalSessions.write`). Prove it on a real chat, and show that context survives and a later prompt continues.
2. **Trusted reminder wake**: how the comms epic's one-shot wake reaches an idle OMP chat (extension hook, fixed reminder text). Can the same path take a different trusted, desktop-originated reminder (pause, resume, shutdown, cap decision) without peer-authored content?
3. **Graceful exit**: how an OMP chat ends itself or is ended cleanly (an extension call, `/exit`, closing stdin), and how long until the process tree is gone (`killPtyTree` as the backstop).
4. **Models and sign-in**: real output of `omp models --json` (signed in) and `omp usage --json`. Record redacted fixtures under `src/main/cults/__fixtures__/`, with emails, account ids and tokens removed. Decide how a cost tier (`low`/`normal`/`high`) is derived from fields OMP declares (pricing, role hints such as smol/slow), never from model names, and how to pass a chosen model (`--model provider/id`, checked with `isSafeModelId`).
5. **Sanctum for project-less cults**: can the app create an app-owned directory under `userData/cults/<cultId>/` and initialize it as a local-mode Dark Mechanicus workspace that is not tracked in the Folders list, so that mailbox endpoints, `issueChatCli` grants and per-folder chat stores work unchanged? List every check that rejects untracked folders (`chatHandlers.trackedFolder`, `launchFolder.resolveLaunchFolder`, grant issuance, the control pipe) and the smallest trusted bypass that admits only a registered sanctum. If this is infeasible, recommend the alternative.
6. **Watch-only terminal**: can `TerminalPane` attach to a PTY with no input path (keystrokes, paste or resize not forwarded), and is resize still needed for rendering?
7. **Role grants and live upgrades**: confirm that an `orchestrator` grant without Allow save, and a `worker` grant, both get mailbox capabilities, and list what else each can change. Then find how an approved petition changes a **running** Magos's access without restarting its CLI: (a) turning on Allow save on its workspace grant, and (b) granting orchestrator access to another tracked folder. DM-619's multi-folder grants for project-less chats are the starting point; `renewChatGrant` and `bindChatGrant` are candidates. Also find how either is revoked when the run ends.
8. **Pipeline sources**: how the desktop can read, as the person, every mailbox message sent between the members of one run, in both directions and in order, using the comms epic's human-only read path. Find whether OMP chat transcripts expose a member's current activity (working or idle via `terminalSessions.busy`, and the last tool call or message) so that the UI can show what each named member is doing.

## Output
`docs/design/cults.md`: a decision record with one section per question (1 to 8), giving the command or API, the evidence (command output excerpts, versions, OS), the decision and the consequences for the later tickets (launch, supervision, models, tools/wake, UI, Shrine). ## Change

- `start(cultId, {timeLimitMs?, cap?})`: create the run, prepare the workspace, start the Magos, and move to `running`.
- **Timer**: one scheduler per active run, with an injectable clock. It fires at `remainingMs`. An unlimited run has no timer. Delays beyond the platform `setTimeout` maximum (about 24.8 days) are re-armed in chunks. Pausing cancels it; resuming reschedules it from the frozen remainder.
- **Pause**: interrupt every member's current turn using the investigation's mechanism (section 1), close the standing wake (`isWakeOpen(runId)` returns false; the wake ticket consumes it), freeze the timer, and deliver a trusted "paused" reminder through the investigation's section 2 path. **Resume** reverses it with a trusted "resumed" reminder.
- **Shutdown** (Stop or expiry):
  1. state `shutting_down`; deliver the trusted shutdown reminder to the Magos;
  2. the run's acolyte grace window (default 3 minutes): acolytes that conclude are ended gracefully;
  3. then the run's Magos window (default 2 minutes) to record the chronicle and conclude;
  4. **hard backstop** at grace + window + 60 s after Stop or expiry: `endMember(..., {graceful:false})` for everything still alive.
  Then: state `ended` with reason `expired` or `stopped`, pending petitions denied, all member grants revoked, including any petition upgrades. The timings come from the run (copied from the cult's defaults, overridable at Start).
- **Kill now**: end every member immediately; reason `killed`.
- **Members**: `addAcolyte` and `dismissAcolyte` enforce state (refused while paused or shutting down) and the cap. A missing or taken name gets a generated themed name (`cultistName`).

  - `allow_save` turns on Allow save for the Magos's workspace grant.

- **Event log**: every summon, dismissal, conclusion, departure, petition and decision, pause and resume, shutdown step and end appends a `cult_events` row with the member's display name.
- **App quit**: end every member and mark active runs `interrupted`. **Startup**: `activeRunsOnStartup()` → mark them `interrupted` and kill any surviving tracked process. ## Context
The archetype contract, store, launcher and commands exist by this point. DM-622 questions 9–10 name the verified target-plan adapter and authority boundary; use that result and never open another project's database directly.

## Change
Create `src/main/cults/planForgeCouncil.ts`:
- bind the run to target epic and starting revision through the verified workspace command layer;
- derive coverage from stored slots, members and reports; require one distinct member/report for each six worker types;
- accept inert reports only from `conclude_service`, capped at 32 KiB and tagged with target revision;
- expose collecting/resolving/valid/stale/invalid and missing worker types;
- before `conclude_run`, re-read the target, reject external change as `target_stale`, require all reports and a Magos synthesis listing accepted/rejected recommendations with reasons, then invoke real draft validation; invalid returns `plan_invalid` without ending;
- confirm the submitted draft revision belongs to the bound target and Magos. Save is not part of this service and remains unavailable until Allow save.

Extend `cultRules.ts`, `cultSupervisor.ts` and control handler only at prerequisite integration points. Other archetypes do not gain this gate.

## Source locations
- `src/core/commands/authoring.ts`; `src/core/services/drafts.ts`; `src/main/desktop/workspacePool.ts`.
- Prerequisite outputs: `docs/design/cults.md`, planned `cultSupervisor.ts`, `cultStore.ts`, `cultRules.ts`, `cultControl.ts`.
- New: `src/main/cults/planForgeCouncil.ts`, `src/main/cults/planForgeCouncil.test.ts`.

The exact adapter is selected by DM-622 evidence. If none is safe, stop and report rather than bypass the workspace API.

## Tests
Use real workspace cores in temporary repositories: six reports unlock validation; every missing role blocks; duplicate coverage does not count; report/synthesis text is inert; external advancement is stale; invalid draft reports errors; valid unsaved draft may conclude; Save fails before Allow save and succeeds only after approval. Extend control/supervisor tests for typed state.

## Collaboration
Ask only the orchestrator. Run targeted tests plus lint and typecheck; full Definition of Done remains at acceptance.

## Revision 5 additive Plan Forge specialists
The Plan Forge gate always requires the fixed six. It also includes every active Magos-created type marked `requiredForConclusion`; each needs a distinct assigned member and report and appears in the synthesis. Optional created types never weaken or block the base quorum. Missing-type errors distinguish fixed from Magos-created requirements.
